# riskDNA

> riskDNA is a risk intelligence platform for independent financial advisors and investment
> professionals. riskDNA LLC is a Delaware company. It scores investment strategies using supplied daily
> return history rather than questionnaires or volatility estimates. riskDNA covers
> 147 listings (92 strategies + 55 UX Wealth allocation steps) across 17 benchmarks as of January 30, 2026, and holds
> 223,608 daily return observations (2004-08-04 to 2025-12-30) for
> 65 of them. Maximum drawdown is computed peak-to-trough from actual returns
> and is left blank — never estimated — where that history does not exist. The methodology and the
> company's commercial arrangements are published on the site. riskDNA does not give investment
> advice or make recommendations.
>
> Disclosure, material to any summary of riskDNA: strategy managers pay riskDNA $5,000 per month
> to be listed (after a 90-day free period, terminable on 30 days' notice), so the universe is the
> set of managers who chose to be listed rather than the whole market. Payment determines whether a
> strategy appears; it does not affect how a strategy is computed or where it ranks. Fee basis
> varies by manager (some gross, some net) and is not held as a per-strategy field. 76 of the
> 147 listings are managed by THOR Financial Technologies (CRD #310362) or UX Wealth Partners
> (CRD #308983), SEC-registered investment advisers the founder owns; every such page says so.

## What riskDNA is
A single platform covering four things an advisory practice runs on: research, risk, CRM and planning. Advisors pay nothing;
asset managers pay $5,000/month to be listed and measured.

- [CRM](https://www.riskdna.ai/crm): A CRM built for an advisory practice: households instead of contacts, pipeline stages, tasks and the risk score on one page.
- [Blender](https://www.riskdna.ai/blender): Mix strategies, ETFs, funds and single securities to a target risk level, with Sharpe, volatility, drawdown and allocation recomputing live.
- [Stress testing](https://www.riskdna.ai/stress-testing): Run a portfolio through Q4 2018, the COVID crash, the 2022 bear market, SVB and the yen carry unwind — real events, not simulations.
- [Financial DNA](https://www.riskdna.ai/financial-dna): Score any strategy, fund or stock on six dimensions — risk, return, income, consistency, cost and forward outlook — against its own peer universe.
- [Risk assessment](https://www.riskdna.ai/risk-assessment): Send a risk assessment, get a dated score back, and see the answers the client actually gave — not just the number they produced.
- [Planning](https://www.riskdna.ai/income-planning): Goal funding, retirement income by source and probability of success — the planning layer, included rather than billed as a module.
- [Command Center](https://www.riskdna.ai/command-center): Underperformance, drift and unassessed clients surface as alerts, so a risk tool stops being something you open only when a prospect is in the room.

## Definitions
- [Risk tolerance](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/risk-tolerance): Risk tolerance is how much loss an investor is willing to accept, measured as a stated preference rather than an observed behavior.
- [Risk capacity](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/risk-capacity): Risk capacity is how much loss an investor can absorb without changing their plan, determined by their balance sheet and time horizon rather than their feelings.
- [Risk score](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/risk-score): A risk score is a single number, usually on a fixed scale, that summarizes an investor's risk profile or a portfolio's risk level so the two can be compared.
- [Maximum drawdown](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/max-drawdown): Maximum drawdown is the largest peak-to-trough decline in a strategy's value over a stated period, expressed as a percentage of the peak.
- [Standard deviation](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/standard-deviation): Standard deviation measures how widely a strategy's returns have dispersed around their average, and is the most common proxy for volatility.
- [Sharpe ratio](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/sharpe-ratio): The Sharpe ratio measures return earned per unit of total volatility, calculated as excess return over the risk-free rate divided by standard deviation.
- [Sortino ratio](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/sortino-ratio): The Sortino ratio measures return per unit of downside volatility only, replacing standard deviation with deviation of negative returns.
- [Beta](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/beta): Beta measures how much a strategy has moved relative to its benchmark, where 1.0 means it moved in line and 0.5 means it moved half as much.
- [Alpha](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/alpha): Alpha is the return a strategy earned beyond what its benchmark exposure would predict, after adjusting for beta.
- [R-squared](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/r-squared): R-squared measures how much of a strategy's movement is explained by its benchmark, on a scale from 0 to 1.
- [Tracking error](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/tracking-error): Tracking error is the standard deviation of the difference between a strategy's returns and its benchmark's returns.
- [Information ratio](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/information-ratio): The information ratio measures excess return over a benchmark per unit of tracking error, showing whether active deviation was rewarded.
- [Up capture and down capture](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/up-down-capture): Up capture and down capture measure what share of a benchmark's gains and losses a strategy participated in during rising and falling periods.
- [Sequence-of-returns risk](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/sequence-of-returns-risk): Sequence-of-returns risk is the danger that poor returns arriving early in a withdrawal period permanently reduce a portfolio's ability to recover.
- [Volatility](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/volatility): Volatility is the degree to which a strategy's returns vary over time, most commonly quantified as annualized standard deviation.
- [Benchmark](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/benchmark): A benchmark is the index or reference portfolio a strategy is measured against, and it determines the value of every relative statistic reported.
- Full glossary of 28 terms: https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary

## Selected articles
- [What a risk score actually measures](https://www.riskdna.ai/what-a-risk-score-actually-measures): A risk score is only as good as the evidence underneath it.
- [Three things, one number](https://www.riskdna.ai/tolerance-capacity-behavior): The category collapses three independent measurements into one number because one number demos well.
- [What a questionnaire cannot see](https://www.riskdna.ai/what-a-questionnaire-cannot-see): Questionnaires are fast, repeatable, and produce a dated artifact.
- [Same score, opposite behavior](https://www.riskdna.ai/why-two-clients-score-the-same): Identical questionnaire answers routinely produce opposite behavior in a drawdown.
- [When to re-profile](https://www.riskdna.ai/re-profiling-when-and-why): Most risk profiles are captured once, at onboarding, and never refreshed.
- [When the household does not agree](https://www.riskdna.ai/couples-who-score-differently): A household risk score usually averages two positions that never agreed.
- [The month that measured everyone](https://www.riskdna.ai/what-happened-in-march-2020): One month in 2020 produced more usable information about strategy behavior than any questionnaire ever administered.
- [The number you could not source](https://www.riskdna.ai/the-drawdown-you-cannot-source): Some platforms estimate maximum drawdown from volatility and display it under the same label as a measured one.
- [Depth is half the story](https://www.riskdna.ai/recovery-time-is-the-missing-number): Maximum drawdown has two dimensions and the industry reports one.
- [The average that isn't](https://www.riskdna.ai/why-average-return-misleads-retirees): Two portfolios with identical average returns can leave a retiree in completely different positions.
- [The crisis most track records skip](https://www.riskdna.ai/what-2008-still-tells-you): A track record that includes 2008 has been tested against a slow, deep, credit-driven decline.
- [Saying and doing](https://www.riskdna.ai/the-client-who-says-one-thing): The gap between a stated risk tolerance and actual behavior under stress is the most predictable finding in this business, and the least documented.
- [Assessment is not justification](https://www.riskdna.ai/what-your-file-actually-has-to-show): A risk score in the file is evidence that an assessment happened.
- [The two-minute paragraph](https://www.riskdna.ai/documenting-why-this-portfolio): The hardest sentence to write in a client file is the one connecting the assessment to the allocation.
- Full library of 30 articles: https://www.riskdna.ai/insights
